newsitem.title: USA: PECO Energy workers reject union.
newsitem.headline: PECO Energy workers reject union.

text.p: - Workers at PECO Energy Co, which is facing the uncertainties of deregulation, voted to reject a union representation drive, a federal labor official said Tuesday.

More than 1,000 employees turned out Monday to reject representation by the Utility Workers of America. The vote was 695 to 228, said Frank Hoeber, acting regional director of the National Labor Relations Board.
Hoeber said another 200 ballots had been challenged, but the number was too small to affect the outcome of the vote.

The Utility Workers Union of America had sought to represent up to 1,100 workers at the Limerick and Peach Bottom nuclear power plants, as well in administrative offices and labs in suburban Valley Forge.
The International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers is also seeking to represent 2,000 employees, mostly repair workers and production staff at fossil-fuel generating stations.
Neil McDermott, a PECO spokesman, called the election "an overwhelming rejection of union representation.
"Our employees obviously concluded after hearing both sides that it was best to remain union-free as we proceed to meet the challenges of a changing era," he said.
None of PECO's 7,000 employees is represented by a union.
A new Pennsylvania law will allow customers to buy power from whatever source offers the best price by the year 2001.
The prospect of competition has created anxieties in an industry that had been protected by regulation and a guaranteed return on investment.
